title: 26 shots of Mt. Fuji
subtitle: My favorite photos of Fuji-san, from my trip to Japan in Nov, 2023.
byline: Photos shot by Rasagy Sharma, and gallery crafted with Claude Code using Mapbox & Python.
footer: May you be blessed by Fuji-san’s view on your next trip to Japan!

chapters.title: A homage to Hokusai
chapters.description: The most popular artworks featuring Mt. Fuji are by the Japanese ukiyo-e artist Hokusai. His series of landscape prints titled “Thirty-six Views of Mount Fuji” are one of the most recognizable work of Japanese art. Inspired by him, I picked 26 shots that I loved, from the hundreds I captured during my trip.

chapters.title: Greeted on arrival by Fuji-san
chapters.description: My favorite part of flying is looking out from the window. So after checking paths of recent HKG to NRT flights, I checked in to a seat on the left side, hoping to get a good view of Japan before I land. I did not expect to be blessed by a view of Mt. Fuji as we got closer to Tokyo!

chapters.title: Bus ride to Fujikawaguchiko
chapters.description: After struggling to spot Mt. Fuji from Tokyo for a few days, I took a bus nearly at noon to stay next to Lake Kawaguchi for one night. I was frantically checking our location & looking out of the window, hoping that it wouldn’t be too cloudy. I caught a few glimpses of Mt. Fuji from the bus as I arrived.

chapters.title: Staring at the night sky with Fuji-san
chapters.description: By 5PM, it was nearly sunset. The temperature fell drastically. The whole town was eerily silent as I strolled around the Lake Kawaguchi, and the night sky shimmered with stars all around Fuji-san.

chapters.title: Dew at dawn
chapters.description: The view from my Ryokan’s rooftop was splendid. By 7AM, Fuji-san was illuminated while the rest of the town didn’t receive direct sunlight yet.

chapters.title: Walk, take a bus, repeat.
chapters.description: Do you know why the bus frequency is low around Lake Kawaguchi? So one can marvel at Fuji-san from different spots without a rush.

chapters.title: Roaming around Lake Kawaguchi
chapters.description: Lake Kawaguchi is the second largest of the Fuji Five Lakes. Spent a few hours in the morning roaming through Momiji Maple Corridor, small shops, shrines & Oishi Park.

chapters.title: Cloudy, with a chance for snow!
chapters.description: By afternoon, clouds gathered around Mt. Fuji. In a few hours, Fuji-san had disappeared in the veil of clouds. I didn’t spot it on my way to Osaka, but was elated to see it on the Shinkansen ride back to Tokyo!

chapters.title: A spectacular farewell
chapters.description: Mt. Fuji is only visible for a few months across the year. I ended the trip feeling blessed for witnessing many splendid views of Fuji-san, only for the flight to offer me one last, breath-taking view. What a memorable trip!
